title: How to test if a value is between two numbers
task: An in-range check — because 10<=A2<=20 doesn't work the way you'd hope.

excel.note: There's no BETWEEN operator; AND of two comparisons is the idiom.

explanation: The chained form 10<=A2<=20 doesn't error — worse, it evaluates left-to-right into TRUE<=20, which is always TRUE, so everything passes the test. AND(A2>=10,A2<=20) is the correct spelling: 15 clears both bounds. An arithmetic alternative some prefer: =MEDIAN(10,A2,20)=A2 is TRUE exactly when A2 is within [10,20] — and MEDIAN(10,A2,20) by itself doubles as a clamp.
